reason: E1 shows that Mo-containing RHEAs retain strength better at high temperature, supporting the first premise. However, the specific claim that Mo addition increases lattice distortion and retards dislocations in TiVNbTa is not directly evidenced; E1 and E2 only describe general trends and do not provide mechanistic data or results for TiVNbTaMo. The assumption that a single-phase BCC structure is maintained with Mo addition is unsupported by the cited passages. Thus, only one key premise is directly supported, while the mechanistic and structural premises lack specific evidence.
premises: Mo-containing RHEAs (MoNbTaW, MoNbTaVW) show lower reduction in yield strength at elevated temperatures compared to other MPEAs.
Increased lattice distortion from Mo addition retards dislocation glide and enhances high-temperature strength.
TiVNbTa baseline is a single-phase BCC alloy with yield strength ~800 MPa at RT and ~330 MPa at 1273 K.
Adding ~5 at.% Mo to TiVNbTa will maintain a single-phase BCC structure.
The strength improvement mechanism in Mo-containing RHEAs is transferable to the TiVNbTa system.
